label: sparse: late copy-phase input j / delimiter (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). About 92% of activation mass is at the delimiter or in the copy phase, and the rate rises steeply toward the end of long sequences (t=16-17, L=9). The largest single component is copy-phase input j (47% of mass), most often when the output is a (j followed by a in the original). Another 19% is at <DEL>, which is enriched when the first token is a. Small remaining mass is spread over other copy inputs (a, c, t, v) and a few late original-phase steps. It never fires at t<3 or on recall_idx 1. No token or position rule I tried is selective: it fires on only about 1-3% of late copy-phase j inputs and about 2% of <DEL> steps in sequences starting with a, so precision stays below 0.26 for every predicate. The recorded predicate (late copy-phase j) covers about 42% of mass at about 2% precision. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.23). Coverage is a bit higher in the top quartile, and the strongest examples are late copy-phase j inputs.
